extracted.intended_audience: Depositors, patent applicants/agents, and collection managers handling Budapest Treaty biological deposits (national culture collections and patent-related depositors).
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and quality/administrative standards for depositing biological material with national culture collections for patent purposes under the Budapest Treaty, including what materials are accepted, technical/packing/quantity requirements, viability testing, notification, sample furnishing, fees and conversion procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of microorganisms accepted (NCIMB)
rubrics_metrics.description: NCIMB accepts bacteria (including actinomycetes), yeasts and bacteriophages up to and including ACDP Group 2 and Class 1 genetically modified microorganisms (GMOs). Class 2 GMOs may be accepted for deposit but this is on a case by case basis only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deposits must be able to withstand preservation by either freeze-drying or freezing over liquid nitrogen without any significant change to their properties. NCIMB reserves the right to refuse material that, in the opinion of the Curator, presents an unacceptable hazard or is technically too difficult to handle. In exceptional circumstances NCIMB may accept deposits which can only be maintained in active culture, by prior negotiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plasmid acceptance criteria (NCIMB)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plasmids, including recombinants, are accepted either (i) cloned into a bacterial or actinomycete host, or (ii) as naked DNA preparations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For (i) the hazard category of the host with or without its plasmid must be no higher than ACDP Group 2. For (ii) the phenotypic markers of the plasmids must be capable of expression in a bacterial or actinomycete host and readily detectable. Physical containment requirements must not be higher than level II as defined by GMAG and properties of the deposited material must not be changed significantly by liquid nitrogen freezing or freeze-drying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of orthodox seeds (NCIMB)
rubrics_metrics.description: NCIMB accepts orthodox seeds i.e. those that can be dried to a low moisture content and stored at -20°C (or lower) without damage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All arable crops and many small seeded tree species produce orthodox seeds. Recalcitrant seeds (e.g., cocoa, rubber, some tropical fruits, large seeded woody species) are not accepted. Acceptance and furnishing of seeds are subject to the Plant Health (Great Britain) Order 1987 and related regulations; notify NCIMB in advance of intended seed deposits to ensure compliance and avoid customs delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant cell/tissue culture acceptance (NCIMB)
rubrics_metrics.description: NCIMB accepts plant cell tissue cultures, either frozen or as active cultures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All relevant regulations should be complied with. NCIMB may accept only on prior notification so it can ensure regulatory compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to refuse hazardous or technically difficult material (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections reserve the right to refuse to accept any material for deposit which, in the opinion of the Curator, presents an unacceptable hazard or is technically too difficult to handle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance may be conditional or refused; exceptional circumstances may allow otherwise unacceptable formats only by prior negotiation and possible extra fees/delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred form and quantity by material type (NCIMB & others)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred replicates/quantities to be supplied vary by material: e.g., NCIMB: Bacteria and yeasts: 2 replicates; Bacteriophages: 2 x 0.5 ml or 1 x 10 ml cell-free lysate (at least 10^8 pfu/ml); Plasmids: 1 x 10 ml DNA at least 20 mcg/ml; Seeds: 250 seeds (with additional guidance on long-term numbers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositor responsible to ensure enough seeds for the life of the deposit. IBPGR recommends minimum 4,000 seeds for long-term storage; USPTO requires minimum 2,500. For plant cell tissue cultures: 25 ampoules (frozen) or multiple active cultures as specified (e.g., 3 suspension cultures or 5 undifferentiated cultures or 10 in vitro plantlets). Avoid agar plate cultures where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viability testing times (NCIMB)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average times for viability testing vary by material: Bacteria and yeasts: 3 days (or up to 14 days); Bacteriophages: 3 days (or up to 5 days); Plasmids: 5 days (longer in slow growing hosts); Seeds and plant cell cultures: depend on type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors should realize testing may take longer in some cases; figures in brackets indicate possible extended durations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositor checks and renewal of stocks (NCIMB & others)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections prepare their own lyophilized/frozen batches from depositor-supplied material and renew stocks as necessary. Depositors may be asked to provide further material to renew diminishing stocks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositor may request a sample of NCIMB-prepared batches for an authenticity check. Collections nevertheless store a portion of the original material supplied by the depositor wherever possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official language requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The official language of the collection is English; communications in any other language are not accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is stated for NCIMB, NIBSC and NRRL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractual obligations of depositor (NCIMB example)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NCIMB application form constitutes a contract binding the depositor to provide all necessary information requested, to pay all necessary fees, to indemnify NCIMB against claims arising from release of samples (unless due to NCIMB negligence), not to withdraw the deposit during required storage, and to authorize NCIMB to furnish samples according to applicable patent requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar contractual terms appear at other collections (NIBSC: provide biohazard statement, material in required form/quantity, pay transportation charges, observe Budapest Treaty terms, indemnify).

rubrics_metrics.name: Import and quarantine regulations compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposits of certain materials (e.g., non-indigenous plant pathogens and certain seeds) may require licenses to be worked with; prospective depositors should contact the collection in advance so necessary arrangements can be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply may result in immediate destruction of submitted material. When responding to requests from abroad, collections assume requesting parties have met import requirements of their country; for UK collections, samples of plant pathogens/seeds requiring permits will not be released until permit confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making the original deposit: required forms and notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositors must complete the collection's accession/deposit form and supply required documents; the receipt and viability statement are issued on mandatory international forms BP/4 and BP/9; attestation of later indication/amendment on BP/8; notification of furnishing samples on BP/14.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections may have their own additional standard forms for acceptance or refusal notices. Unofficial provisional notifications (date/accession) may be given before official receipt is issued but are provisional pending viability testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Converting previous (non-Treaty) deposits to Budapest Treaty deposits
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposits made outside Budapest Treaty may be converted by the original depositor to Treaty deposits; however, deposits previously made for scientific purposes and already generally available may require authorization for continued availability or else a new deposit must be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deposits previously made free of charge are subject on conversion to the storage fees normally levied. Administrative requirements for conversion are generally the same as for original deposits, with noted exceptions (e.g., shipping procedures may not apply). NRRL does not permit conversion of deposits not originally made for patent purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making a new deposit: required international forms
rubrics_metrics.description: For a new deposit the depositor may be required to complete BP/2 (or the collection's model form) and supply the documents/declarations required by Rule 6.2; the receipt and viability statement for a new deposit are issued on BP/5 and BP/9 respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some collections do not require a standard form for new deposits but ask for acknowledgement that new deposit is same as original (NRRL).

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice and provision of request forms to third parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections differ: NCIMB and NCYC advise third parties of correct procedures and will provide model request form BP/12 or forms supplied by industrial property offices; NIBSC does not advise requesting parties or supply request forms except that they must be obtained from the relevant industrial property office; NRRL supplies EPO form for EPO-regulated requests only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proof of entitlement is required, collections may provide or point to model forms. Collections assume requestors have met their own import requirements when responding to overseas requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on furnishing samples
rubrics_metrics.description: Samples are furnished only from batches prepared by the collection (e.g., NCIMB furnishes bacteria from its own preparations; plasmids and seeds from depositor-supplied material). Samples of potentially hazardous microorganisms or those requiring permits are withheld until the requesting party has appropriate containment facilities or permits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Samples are delivered only to recognized microbiological laboratories and not to private addresses (NCIMB). Requesting parties must be “skilled in the art” before microorganisms are shipped (NRRL).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to depositor when samples furnished
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositors are notified (typically by model form BP/14 or by letter) when samples of their microorganism have been furnished to third parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections (NCIMB, NCYC, NIBSC) use BP/14 or their own model forms to inform the depositor; some use individual letters for certain notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cataloguing/listing Budapest Treaty deposits
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies vary: NCYC does not list Treaty deposits in its published catalog; NCIMB lists Treaty deposits only with the specific written authorization of the depositor; NIBSC does not list Treaty deposits in its published catalogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositor consent or explicit authorization is required for public listing at some collections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of fees and VAT
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections publish schedules of fees for storage, issuance of viability statements, furnishing of samples (plus carriage/packaging/expedition costs for overseas destinations), issuance of certification, and administration fees for amendments. Fees are payable to the collection and, where applicable, subject to Value Added Tax at the current rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where statutory provisions require the collection to obtain a license or certificate prior to accepting certain deposits (e.g., seeds), the actual cost of obtaining such license/certificate will be charged to the depositor. High containment processing may incur higher charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for depositors availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections vary in providing guidance: NCYC does not produce standard guidance notes; NCIMB publishes a leaflet containing guidance notes; NIBSC provides guidance on the deposit form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors should consult the collection's published guidance leaflets or contact the collection for specific shipment and documentation advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIBSC-specific human and animal cell line technical requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Human and animal cell material must be cryopreserved cultures; minimum number of replicates is 12. Deposits must contain at least 1 x 10^6 viable cells per ampoule for monolayer or suspension cultures; for colony fragments at least 4 colony fragments per ampoule. Where a feeder cell layer is required, a sample sufficient to support testing must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Human embryonic stem cell deposits are subject to current UK regulations and may require additional applications (e.g., UK Steering Committee). Materials must be packed to maintain cryopreserved state in transit; insufficient dry ice/packing may lead to refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIBSC processing and biosafety review requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: No patent deposit should be sent to NIBSC without a Biohazard Risk Assessment having been first received and reviewed by NIBSC. For genetically modified cell lines this will include a formal review by the NIBSC Biological Safety Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material requiring handling at Containment Levels higher than Level 2 may require a longer completion period and higher charges to reflect increased costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIBSC stock renewal policy
rubrics_metrics.description: NIBSC does not prepare its own batch of deposited microorganisms; when stock originally provided by the depositor has been depleted, the depositor will be asked to provide a new deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For some human stem cell lines, transfer from the UK Stem Cell Bank to NIBSC patent deposit may be possible, subject to authenticity checks by the depositor.

rubrics_metrics.name: NRRL: excluded organisms and materials
rubrics_metrics.description: NRRL excludes a long list of taxa and materials (e.g., many pathogenic genera including Bacillus anthracis, Brucella, Clostridium species, Mycobacterium tuberculosis, viral/Rickettsial/Chlamydial agents, agents requiring permits, mixtures of microorganisms, phages not in microorganisms, monoclonal antibodies, cell lines, plasmids not inserted in microorganisms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fastidious microorganisms requiring more than reasonable attention for lyophilization are excluded. This explicit exclusion list defines what NRRL will not accept.

rubrics_metrics.name: NRRL acceptance of recombinant strains conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Recombinant strains, strains containing recombinant DNA, plasmid-bearing strains, and strains containing viruses are accepted only if the deposit document includes a clear statement that progeny of the strains can be processed at Physical Containment Level P1 or less and meet NIH Guidelines (as applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance contingent on compliance with U.S. DHHS/NIH recombinant DNA guidelines and any subsequent revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: NRRL form/contract and depositor responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: By completing the NRRL deposition form the depositor surrenders any right to withdraw the deposit during required storage, accepts NRRL policy on handling/distribution, and accepts responsibility for authenticity of NRRL preparations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NRRL does not enter into a separate written contract; the deposition form serves as acknowledgment of these responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: NRRL stock preparation and authenticity checks
rubrics_metrics.description: NRRL stores and distributes lyophilized material supplied by the depositor if so requested, or makes its own lyophilized preparations by subculture. NRRL requires the depositor to check authenticity of its lyophilized preparations and record results on the viability statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the depositor does not report authenticity test results within three months, NRRL assumes its preparations are equivalent to the original deposit.

rubrics_metrics.name: NRRL policy on conversion and new deposits
rubrics_metrics.description: NRRL does not permit conversion of deposits not originally made for patent purposes to Budapest Treaty deposits. Administrative requirements for converting a deposit previously made for patent purposes are the same as for an original deposit except no fee is payable. NRRL does not require a standard form for making a new deposit but asks for an acknowledgement that the new deposit is the same as the original and copies of relevant documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural differences between collections should be checked prior to attempting conversion or new deposit.

rubrics_metrics.name: NRRL viability testing times (NRRL-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average viability testing times at NRRL: Bacteria 3 days (or up to 15 days); Fungi 10 days (or up to 15 days); Yeasts 10 days (or up to 20 days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors should expect possible extended testing durations in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions and documentation for overseas requests
rubrics_metrics.description: When responding to requests from abroad, collections assume requesting parties have met import requirements for their country; requesting parties may be required to provide import documentation or permits before samples are released.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections will withhold distribution until permit/containment verification is confirmed for controlled organisms; some collections require shipment only to recognized microbiological laboratories and not to private addresses.
